text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The cost of building a double-storey mansion for Harare's executive mayor, originally budgeted at Z$5 million, will escalate to as much as Z$14 million upon completion, the Zimbabwe Independent learnt this week.
- Southampton Life of South Africa is currently entertaining advances by two suitors for its 49 percent stake in Zimbabwe insurance company Southampton Assurance.
- The Zimbabwean government is owed Z$514.4 million in Commodity Import Programme repayments by 124 companies, both local and international, operating in the country.
- The much-awaited tender for Zimbabwe's second cellular phone network has been awarded to Telecel, a consortium of foreigners and a company made up of local groups and individuals.

- The International Monetary Fund is willing to establish a new lending programme with Zimbabwe, a country it views as one of Africa's brightest economic prospects, says leading commercial bank, Barclays Zimbabwe.
- Zimbabwe's Indegenous (black) Commercial Farmers Union has secured a seasonal Z$100 million loan from the United Merchant Bank to finance tobacco growers in the current agricultural season.
